**Priorities of any orderable type**: A priority store ranks items by a number, a string, a tuple or any value that can be ordered.

API details

- **SimPy:** `resources.store.PriorityItem`

- **Builder:** `put={"store": "queue", "priority": (1, "urgent")}`
- **Low-level:** `simpy.PriorityItem((1, "urgent"), item)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c5_priority_item_storage_any_orderable_type`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c5_priority_store.py), [`test_c5_priority_yaml_list_literal`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c5_priority_store.py), [`test_c5_priority_mixed_types_raise_type_error`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c5_priority_store.py)
- **Taught on:** [Priorities of any orderable type](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/stores-and-containers/#start-with-items-and-serve-by-priority)

## C6: Run Control

Starting a run from a given time and state, reading the current time, ending it at a time, at an event or on a condition and reading the value that ended it, draining it, running it in segments, stepping through it one model event at a time, scheduling an event with a priority, an environment class of your own, and the pace of the run: its factor, strict pacing and syncing with the wall clock.

**Initial time**: The simulation clock starts at a given time instead of 0.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment(initial_time=...)`
- **YAML:** `simulation.initial_time`
- **Builder:** `SimulationContext(..., initial_time=100)`
- **Low-level:** `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(initial_time=100)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_initial_time`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_run_control.py)
- **Taught on:** [Initial time](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#initial-time)

**Initial resources**: Each resource starts with a given number of units.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.resources.resource.Resource(capacity=...)`
- **YAML:** `resources.<name>.current_cap`
- **Builder:** `add_resource(name, current_cap=2, ...)`
- **Low-level:** `CapacityConfig(current_cap=2, ...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_initial_resources`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_initial_state.py)
- **Taught on:** [Initial resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#initial-time)

**Initial inventory**: Containers start with a given level, and stores with given items.

API details

- **SimPy:** `Container(init=...)`; items in a `Store`
- **YAML:** `containers.<name>.level` and `stores.<name>.items`
- **Builder:** `add_container(..., level=6)` and `add_store(..., items=[...])`
- **Low-level:** `ContainerConfig(level=6)` and `DynamicStore(..., items=[...])`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_initial_inventory`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_initial_state.py)
- **Taught on:** [Initial inventory](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/stores-and-containers/#start-with-items-and-serve-by-priority)

**Initial entity state**: Each arriving entity, such as an order, starts with given attributes.

API details

- **SimPy:** the attributes a process starts with
- **YAML:** `arrivals.<name>.attributes`
- **Builder:** `add_arrival(..., attributes={...})`
- **Low-level:** the values a process is started with
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_initial_entity_state`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_initial_state.py)
- **Taught on:** [Initial entity state](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/task-flow/#attributes)

**Stop at a time**: The run ends at a given simulation time.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.run(until=...)`
- **YAML:** `run.until`
- **Builder:** `app.run(until=...)`
- **Low-level:** `env.run(until=...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_stop_at_a_time`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_run_control.py)
- **Taught on:** [Stop at a time](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#run-length_1)

**Stop at an event**: The run ends when a given event happens, such as a closing signal, even before its end time.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.run(until=event)`
- **YAML:** `run.stop: {signal: closing}` beside `run.until`
- **Builder:** `app.run(until=..., stop={"signal": "closing"})`, a signal's name, or a function returning an event
- **Low-level:** `env.run(until=event)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_stop_at_an_event`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_stop_at_an_event_at_the_same_instant_as_until`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Difference:** When the stop and `until` fall at the same time, `until` ends the run first, as SimPy's own `until` would.
- **Taught on:** [Stop at an event](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#stop-early)

**Explicit stop condition**: The run ends as soon as a condition on the model's state holds.

API details

- **SimPy:** `env.run(until=event)` with a process that succeeds the event when the condition holds
- **YAML:** `run.stop: {condition: level.stock >= 5}`
- **Builder:** `app.run(until=..., stop={"condition": "..."})`
- **Low-level:** `env.watch_changes(check)` and `env.run(until=event)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_explicit_stop_condition`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Taught on:** [Explicit stop condition](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#stop-early)

**Stop arrivals and drain**: New arrivals stop, and the run goes on until everything already in the model has finished.

API details

- **SimPy:** interrupt the source, then `env.run(until=env.all_of(entities))`
- **YAML:** `run.drain: true` or `{limit: 1 h}`; `desflow run --drain`
- **Builder:** `app.run(until=..., drain=True)`, or `context.stop_arrivals()`
- **Low-level:** `source.interrupt()`, then `env.run(until=env.all_of(processes))`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_stop_arrivals_and_drain`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_stop_arrivals_and_drain_with_a_limit`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Taught on:** [Stop arrivals and drain](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#drain)

**Step one event**: The run advances one event at a time, so a script can watch each step.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.step()`
- **YAML:** `SimulationContext.from_yaml(path).start()`, then `.step()`
- **Builder:** `app.start()`, `app.step()`, `app.close()`
- **Low-level:** `env.step()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_step_one_event`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Difference:** A blueprint has no stepping key; its context, from `from_yaml`, steps as a builder context does.
- **Taught on:** [Step one event](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#step-and-peek)

**Inspect next event time**: A script reads when the next event will happen without running it.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.peek()`
- **YAML:** `SimulationContext.from_yaml(path).start()`, then `.peek()`
- **Builder:** `app.peek()`
- **Low-level:** `env.peek()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_inspect_next_event_time`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Taught on:** [Inspect next event time](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#step-and-peek)

**A step processes only the model's events**: `step()` and `peek()` count the events of the model, not the statistics, flush, lag, ingress and watcher processes that desflow adds, so a script steps a model as it would step it in SimPy. Inside `run()` the step processes every event, desflow's own included, because SimPy's `run()` calls `step()` for each event in its one queue.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.step()` and `peek()`
- **YAML:** `SimulationContext.from_yaml(path).start()`, then `.step()` and `.peek()`; `processes:` entries are model events
- **Builder:** `app.start()`, `app.step()`, `app.peek()`; `add_process` functions are model events
- **Low-level:** `env.step()` and `env.peek()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_step_counts_model_events`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_step_counts_model_events_in_arrival_models`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_step_with_a_live_capacity_change`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_step_with_a_task_that_has_on_actions`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_run_after_steps_gives_the_records_of_one_run`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_finish_after_steps_that_reached_until`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_finish_after_steps_to_until_with_statistics_due_there`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Difference:** With only desflow's own events left, `step()` raises `EmptySchedule` and `peek()` gives infinity, but the queue is not empty: `run()` and `finish()` still process those events.
- **Taught on:** [A step processes only the model's events](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#step-and-peek)

**Value of a run stopped at an event**: `run()` returns the value of the event that stopped it, and raises the exception of a stop that failed. The value is a signal's payload for a stop on a signal, True for a condition, and the event's own value for a function. It is None when `until` or a drain ends the run, or when `until` and the stop are due together. A stop on a signal that fails raises `SignalFailed`, the exception the failed event carries, which is what SimPy raises. The run closes before it returns, so the sinks have their records.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.core.Environment.run(until=event)`
- **YAML:** `SimulationContext.from_yaml(path).run()` returns the value; `desflow run` exits with an error when the stop failed
- **Builder:** `app.run(until=..., stop=...)` and `app.finish()` return the value
- **Low-level:** `env.run(until=event)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_run_value`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py)
- **Taught on:** [Value of a run stopped at an event](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#stop-early)

**Current time**: `t` is the simulation clock, read in a condition or an expression, so a route or a balk can depend on the current time.

API details

- **SimPy:** `core.Environment.now`
- **YAML:** `t` in a condition, such as `t < 110`
- **Builder:** `context.env.now`
- **Low-level:** `env.now`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_current_time`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_run_control.py)
- **Taught on:** [Current time](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#read-the-current-time)

**Schedule an event with a priority**: `env.schedule(event, priority, delay)` puts an event on the queue, and a `fire` action with `after` fires a one-shot signal that many seconds from now, as SimPy's `schedule` does.

API details

- **SimPy:** `core.Environment.schedule`
- **YAML:** `fire: {signal: s, after: 5 s}` on a signal with `once: true`
- **Builder:** `{"fire": {"signal": "s", "after": 5}}` in `on=`, or `context.env.schedule(event, priority, delay)`
- **Low-level:** `env.schedule(event, priority, delay)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_schedule_with_a_priority`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_environment.py), [`test_c6_fire_with_after_is_not_counted_by_a_drain`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_environment.py), [`test_c6_fire_twice_with_after_is_refused_as_a_one_shot_signal`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_environment.py)
- **Taught on:** [Schedule an event with a priority](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/signals-and-waiting/#actions-when-an-event-happens)

**Urgent and normal event priorities**: An urgent event is processed before the normal events at its time, as SimPy's `URGENT` and `NORMAL` order them; `urgent: true` on a `fire` action resumes the waiters first.

API details

- **SimPy:** `events.URGENT`, `events.NORMAL`
- **YAML:** `fire: {signal: s, urgent: true}` on a signal with `once: true`
- **Builder:** `{"fire": {"signal": "s", "urgent": True}}` in `on=`, or `simpy.events.URGENT` in `context.env.schedule`
- **Low-level:** `env.schedule(event, URGENT)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_fire_with_urgent_and_after`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_environment.py), [`test_c6_fire_urgent_and_after_need_a_one_shot_signal`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_environment.py)
- **Taught on:** [Urgent and normal event priorities](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/signals-and-waiting/#actions-when-an-event-happens)

**Run in segments**: `advance(until)` runs a started run to a time or an event and returns with the run open, and `finish()` runs on to the end; the segments give the records of one run. `resume_pacing()` paces again from `now` after a pause.

API details

- **SimPy:** `core.Environment.run`, called again
- **YAML:** `app = SimulationContext.from_yaml(file)`, then `app.start()`, `app.advance(until)` and `app.finish()`
- **Builder:** `app.start()`, `app.advance(until)`, `app.finish()`
- **Low-level:** `env.run(until=)`, called again; `env.resume_pacing()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_stopped_and_resumed_run`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_run_in_segments`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_advance_refuses_what_a_segment_cannot_do`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_segments_with_stop_and_drain_give_the_records_of_one_run`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_step_after_a_segment_processes_its_event_as_simpy_does`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_advance_to_an_event_and_on`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_finish_raises_a_failed_stop_that_advance_reached`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_advance_to_events_adds_one_internal_event_to_the_queue`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_end_conditions.py), [`test_c6_resume_pacing`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_pacing.py)
- **Taught on:** [Run in segments](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#run-in-segments)

**Subclass the environment**: A subclass of `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment` runs the model, so an override of `step` or `schedule` sees its events, as a subclass of SimPy's `Environment` does.

API details

- **SimPy:** `core.Environment`
- **YAML:** `simulation: {environment: !python module.Env}`
- **Builder:** `SimulationContext(environment=Env)`
- **Low-level:** `class Env(DynamicRealtimeEnvironment)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_environment_subclass`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_environment.py), [`test_c6_environment_subclass_in_run`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_environment.py)
- **Taught on:** [Subclass the environment](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/blueprints/#run-on-your-own-environment)

**Real-time factor**: `factor` sets how many real seconds one simulation second takes, so a run paces to the wall clock, as SimPy's RealtimeEnvironment does.

API details

- **SimPy:** `rt.RealtimeEnvironment(factor)`
- **YAML:** `simulation.factor`
- **Builder:** `SimulationContext(factor=)`
- **Low-level:** `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_real_time_factor`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_pacing.py)
- **Taught on:** [Real-time factor](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/clocks-and-pacing/#factor)

**Strict pacing**: With `strict` on, a paced step more than `factor` seconds behind the wall clock raises `RuntimeError`, as SimPy's `RealtimeEnvironment(strict=True)` does.

API details

- **SimPy:** `rt.RealtimeEnvironment.strict`
- **YAML:** `simulation.strict`
- **Builder:** `SimulationContext(strict=True)`
- **Low-level:** `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(strict=True)`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_strict_raises_when_behind`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_pacing.py)
- **Taught on:** [Strict pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/clocks-and-pacing/#strict-pacing)

**Strict by default**: The low-level environment is strict unless `strict=False` is passed, as SimPy's is; the builder and YAML default to off.

API details

- **SimPy:** `rt.RealtimeEnvironment(strict=True)`
- **YAML:** `simulation.strict`, default `false`
- **Builder:** `SimulationContext(strict=False)`, the default
- **Low-level:** `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(strict=True)`, the default
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_strict_default`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_pacing.py)
- **Taught on:** [Strict by default](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/clocks-and-pacing/#strict-pacing)

**Sync with the wall clock**: `sync()` resets only the wall-clock anchor (`real_start`), as SimPy's does, so strict stops counting the time before it. Going on after a pause with the pace kept needs `resume_pacing()`, which also moves the simulation anchor.

API details

- **SimPy:** `rt.RealtimeEnvironment.sync`
- **YAML:** not in YAML: `app.start()`, then `app.env.sync()`
- **Builder:** `app.env.sync()` after `start()`; the builder syncs once when it builds a strict run
- **Low-level:** `env.sync()`
- **Checks:** [`test_c6_sync_catches_up`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c6_pacing.py)
- **Taught on:** [Sync with the wall clock](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/clocks-and-pacing/#strict-pacing)

## C7: Patience

Customers who give up after waiting too long (reneging) and customers who do not join a queue that is too long (balking).

**Reneging**: A customer leaves the queue after waiting longer than their patience.

API details

- **SimPy:** `simpy.events.AnyOf` of a request and a timeout
- **YAML:** `patience: 3 min` on a task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(..., patience=180)`
- **Low-level:** `yield req | env.timeout(patience)`, then `req.triggered`
- **Checks:** [`test_c7_reneging`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py), [`test_c7_reneging_tie_timeout_scheduled_after_the_grant`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py), [`test_c7_reneging_tie_timeout_scheduled_before_the_grant`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py), [`test_c7_reneged_request_leaves_the_queue`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py), [`test_c7_patience_pauses_during_service`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py)
- **Taught on:** [Reneging](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/shop-logic/patience/#leave-after-a-wait)

**Balking**: A customer does not join the queue at all when a condition holds, such as the queue being too long.

API details

- **SimPy:** a check before `Resource.request`
- **YAML:** `balk: <condition>` on a task
- **Builder:** `@app.task(..., balk="...")`
- **Low-level:** an `if` before the request
- **Checks:** [`test_c7_balking`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py), [`test_c7_a_balk_condition_gives_back_the_unit_the_task_kept`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_c7_patience.py)
- **Taught on:** [Balking](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/shop-logic/patience/#refuse-to-join)

## S1: Breakdowns

A resource that fails and is repaired, with the work it interrupts.

**Breakdown and repair**: A resource fails from time to time and is repaired, interrupting the work it was doing.

API details

- **SimPy:** a repair process holding the machine on a `PreemptiveResource`
- **YAML:** `resources.<name>.breakdown: {time_to_failure, repair, work}`
- **Builder:** `add_breakdown(resource, time_to_failure={...}, repair={...}, work=...)`
- **Low-level:** `run_breakdowns(env, resource, sampler, work=...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_s1_failure_during_service`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_s1_breakdowns.py), [`test_s1_failure_during_service_work_finishes`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_s1_breakdowns.py), [`test_s1_planned_change_during_repair`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_s1_breakdowns.py)
- **Difference:** The resource is down on a calendar clock, from the failure to the repair, even while it waits for the work in service to finish with `work: finish`.
- **Taught on:** [Breakdown and repair](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/modelling/breakdowns/#steps)

## S2: Schedules

A schedule of times at which an arrival rate or a capacity changes during a run.

**Finite schedules**: Arrival rates or capacities change at set times during the run.

API details

- **SimPy:** a process that changes values at set times, started before the others
- **YAML:** `scenario` steps with `at`, `path` and `value`
- **Builder:** `add_scenario(steps)` or `add_step(at, path=..., value=...)`
- **Low-level:** `run_scenario(env, steps, until=...)`
- **Checks:** [`test_s2_step_at_an_arrival_time`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_s2_schedules.py)
- **Difference:** A step applies before every other event at its time, so the arrival gap drawn then uses the new value.
- **Taught on:** [Finite schedules](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/modelling/time-varying-arrivals/#boundaries)

## S3: Replay

Arrivals read from a local CSV or Parquet file instead of drawn at random.

**Local replay**: Arrivals come from rows in a local CSV or Parquet file instead of a random distribution.

API details

- **SimPy:** a loop over recorded rows, each a timeout to its time
- **YAML:** `arrivals.<name>.replay: {path, time, unit, fields, on_invalid}`
- **Builder:** `add_arrival_replay(name, source, ...)`
- **Low-level:** `read_trace(source, ...)` and a SimPy loop over its rows
- **Checks:** [`test_s3_replay_equal_times_invalid_rows_and_the_horizon`](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v0.27.0/tests/conformance/test_s3_replay.py)
- **Taught on:** [Local replay](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/inputs/local-replay/#replay-the-rows)

## Differences Kept by Design

- **A run with no until** (SimPy: `core.Environment.run()` returns when no event is left): A run with a sink or an ingress connector and no `until` runs for ever, because a live run has no end: the connectors keep events coming. Give it an `until`, with a `drain` when it should finish its work, or a `stop` that is sure to happen, or stop it with Ctrl+C.
- **Strict pacing at factor 0** (SimPy: `rt.RealtimeEnvironment(factor=0, strict=True)` raises once the wall clock has moved): An unpaced run has no wall clock to fall behind, so SimPy's check at factor 0 would raise on the first step of every unpaced script. `strict` is never checked at factor 0, also before `go_live_at`. **Taught on:** [Strict pacing at factor 0](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/clocks-and-pacing/#strict-pacing)
- **Capacity 0** (SimPy: `resources.resource.Resource(capacity=0)` raises `ValueError`, and so do `Store` and `Container`): A resource, store or container may have a capacity of 0, at the start or later, because its capacity changes during a run: a shift with no packers, a shelf that is closed. At capacity 0 a resource grants no request, and a store or container accepts no put, until the capacity rises; a get still takes what a store or container holds.
# Reference

# YAML Keys

Every key a blueprint file takes, generated from the JSON Schema that ships with desflow. [YAML Blueprints](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/blueprints/index.md) explains how a file is read. [Set Up Your Editor](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/tools/set-up-your-editor/index.md) shows how to have your editor complete and check these keys as you type.

Each section below is a top-level key. A table lists the keys that an entry of it takes, and a section follows for each entry nested in it. Where a value is a number, a whole number, `true` or `false`, or one of a fixed set of names, a `${VAR}` or `${VAR:-default}` reference is also accepted, and a duration such as `5 min` is accepted where the type says Duration.

## simulation

Type: mapping. Required.

The `simulation` section: the arguments of `SimulationContext`.

`logical_start_time` and `go_live_at` take `now`, a signed duration from now such as `-1d` or `-10m`, an ISO datetime, or a `!python` datetime. Both read the same `now`, the moment the file is validated, so `-10m` and `now` are exactly ten minutes apart. `now` and a time without an offset are read in `timezone`, an IANA name, UTC by default.

`strict` makes a paced step raise `RuntimeError` when the run is more than `factor` seconds behind the wall clock; it is False here and never checked at `factor` 0. `environment` is a subclass of `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment` the run is built on.

| Key                  | Type               | Default  |
| -------------------- | ------------------ | -------- |
| `sim_id`             | text               | required |
| `factor`             | number             | `1.0`    |
| `random_seed`        | integer            | none     |
| `timezone`           | text               | none     |
| `logical_start_time` | Time               | none     |
| `go_live_at`         | Time               | none     |
| `warmup`             | number or Duration | none     |
| `initial_time`       | number or Duration | `0.0`    |
| `lag_interval`       | number or Duration | none     |
| `strict`             | boolean            | `false`  |
| `environment`        | !python reference  | none     |

## resources

Type: mapping of names to [Resource](#resources). Optional.

A `resources` entry: its capacity, the order its queue is served in, whether a request of a lower priority value preempts a user, how many requests may wait, the class it is built from, and how it breaks down.

`current_cap` defaults to 1 and `max_cap` to `current_cap`, so `{}` is a resource of one unit. `.inf` makes a resource with no limit. `type` is a `!python` subclass of `ResourceBase`.

| Key           | Type                    | Default  |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | -------- |
| `current_cap` | number                  | none     |
| `max_cap`     | number                  | none     |
| `queue`       | text                    | `"fifo"` |
| `preempt`     | boolean                 | `false`  |
| `queue_limit` | integer                 | none     |
| `type`        | !python reference       | none     |
| `breakdown`   | [Breakdown](#breakdown) | none     |

### Breakdown

A resource's `breakdown`: the time to each failure, the repair time, and whether the tasks being served are interrupted or finish.

| Key               | Type                      | Default       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------- | ------------- |
| `time_to_failure` | [Distribution](#services) | required      |
| `repair`          | [Distribution](#services) | required      |
| `work`            | `interrupt` or `finish`   | `"interrupt"` |

## containers

Type: mapping of names to [Container](#containers). Optional.

A `containers` entry: its capacity, the largest level, its starting level and the class it is built from.

`current_cap` defaults to `max_cap`, and with neither the container has no limit; `.inf` is no limit too. `max_cap` defaults to `current_cap`. `type` is a `!python` subclass of `ContainerBase`.

| Key           | Type              | Default |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ------- |
| `current_cap` | number            | none    |
| `max_cap`     | number            | none    |
| `level`       | integer or number | `0`     |
| `type`        | !python reference | none    |

## stores

Type: mapping of names to [Store](#stores). Optional.

A `stores` entry: how many items it holds, whether it serves by priority, the items it holds when the run starts, and the class it is built from.

`current_cap` defaults to `max_cap`, and with neither the store has no limit; `.inf` is no limit too. `max_cap` defaults to `current_cap`. A capacity is a whole number or `.inf`. `items` are returned in the order given; a priority store's items are `[priority, item]` pairs. `type` is a `!python` subclass of `StoreBase`, which sets its own order, so it cannot be given with `priority`.

| Key           | Type              | Default |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ------- |
| `current_cap` | number            | none    |
| `max_cap`     | number            | none    |
| `priority`    | boolean           | `false` |
| `items`       | list of any value |         |
| `type`        | !python reference | none    |

Time-valued parameters (`mean`, `std`, `low`, `mode`, `high`, `scale`, `value`, and an `empirical`'s `values` and `edges`) take seconds or a duration such as `5 min`; `rate` is a number per second.

| `high`    | number or Duration         | none     |
| `mode`    | number or Duration         | none     |
| `shape`   | number                     | none     |
| `scale`   | number or Duration         | none     |
| `values`  | list of number or Duration | none     |
| `weights` | list of number             | none     |
| `edges`   | list of number or Duration | none     |
| `counts`  | list of number             | none     |

### Replay

An arrival's `replay`: the rows of a local file, each one arrival at its time.

`path` is a CSV or Parquet file, relative to the blueprint; `time` its column of times; `unit` `ms`, `s`, `min` or `h` from the start of the run, or `timestamp` for a date and time read from `simulation.logical_start_time`; `fields` the columns each entity carries, or `all`; `on_invalid` `error` or `skip` for a row with no valid time.

| `on_invalid` | `error` or `skip`                          | `"error"` |

## signals

Type: mapping of names to [SignalSpec](#signals) or list of names. Optional.

A `signals` entry in the mapping form: `{closing: {once: true, on: [...]}}`.

`once` makes the signal fire once, as SimPy's `Event` does; `on` lists actions run when the signal fires, as a task's `on` lists actions run when it ends.

| `once` | boolean                     | `false` |
| `on`   | list of [OnEntry](#onentry) |         |

One entry of an `on:` list: exactly one of a fire, spawn or interrupt action, or a `path` with a `value` as a scenario step sets a registry value.

| `spawn`     | [SpawnAction](#spawnaction)         | none    |
| `interrupt` | [InterruptAction](#interruptaction) | none    |
| `path`      | text                                | none    |
| `value`     | None                                | none    |

### FireAction

An `on:` fire action: fire `signal` with a literal `value`, or with the outcome `from` copies from a signal or a task. `urgent` and `after` fire a one-shot signal ahead of the other events at its time, or later, as SimPy's `env.schedule(event, priority, delay)` does.

| Key      | Type               | Default  |
| -------- | ------------------ | -------- |
| `signal` | text               | required |
| `value`  | None               | none     |
| `from`   | text               | none     |
| `urgent` | boolean            | `false`  |
| `after`  | number or Duration | none     |

| ------- | ------------------ | -------- |

## tasks

Type: mapping of names to [Task](#tasks). Optional.

A `tasks` entry, built with `SimulationContext.task`.

`payload` is the value of the `finished` event: a mapping, or a `!python` function called as `payload(task_id, context)`. `id_field` adds the task id to a mapping payload under that key, `item_field` adds the item its store `get` took, and `attributes` adds the named entity attributes. A task with a `service` and no `resource` is a timed step; one with neither, and no `get`, emits its payload as soon as it is spawned.

`priority` is a number or an expression such as `attr.priority`, for a resource whose `queue` is `priority`. `patience` is seconds, a duration such as `30 s` or an expression; `balk` is a condition checked before the task joins the queue. `resource` is one resource or a list, acquired in the order listed; `keep` hands units to the next task. `on_interrupt` is `resume`, `restart` or `abandon`, and `interrupt` interrupts the running instances of a task when this one finishes. `wait` is what the task waits for first: a signal, a child task, a timeout or a condition, or any or all of several. `signal` names a signal the task fires when it finishes. `fail` is a condition checked after the service: when it holds the task publishes `failed` with `fail_reason`, and goes to `on_fail`. `get` and `put` take from and add to a store or container. `next` is a task name, `when` rules or `weights`. `set` gives the entity attribute values when the task finishes.

| Key                 | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Default    |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `service`           | text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `resource`          | text or list of text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `payload`           | mapping or !python reference                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | required   |
| `id_field`          | text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `item_field`        | text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `attributes`        | list of text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |            |
| `priority`          | number or text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | none       |
| `patience`          | number or text or Duration or expression                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | none       |
| `balk`              | text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `get`               | [TransferStep](#transferstep)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | none       |
| `put`               | [TransferStep](#transferstep)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | none       |
| `next`              | text or [Next](#next)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | none       |
| `set`               | mapping                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |            |
| `wait`              | [SignalWait](#signalwait) or [TaskWait](#taskwait) or [TimeoutWait](#timeoutwait) or [ConditionWait](#conditionwait) or [AnyWait](#anywait) or [AllWait](#allwait) or [AtLeastWait](#atleastwait) or [RequestWait](#requestwait) or [GetWait](#getwait) or [PutWait](#putwait) or [RunningWait](#runningwait) | none       |
| `signal`            | text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `fail`              | text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `fail_reason`       | text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `on_fail`           | text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `keep`              | list of text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |            |
| `preempt`           | boolean                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `true`     |
| `on_interrupt`      | `resume` or `restart` or `abandon`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `"resume"` |
| `on_interrupt_next` | text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | none       |
| `interrupt`         | [InterruptAction](#interruptaction)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | none       |
| `spawn`             | [SpawnAction](#spawnaction)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | none       |
| `subscribe`         | mapping                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | none       |
| `on`                | list of [OnEntry](#onentry)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |            |

### TransferStep

A task's `get` or `put`: one `container` with an `amount`, or one `store`.

`amount` is a number or an expression such as `payload.quantity`, and 1 when it is left out. `priority` is for a put into a priority store, lowest served first, and 0 when it is left out. Text is an expression such as `attr.priority`; any other value is used as written: a number, a list (which orders element by element, as a tuple does), a mapping, null, a date or a bool. `filter` is a condition for a store get, such as `item.size == attr.size`, where `item.<field>` reads the item offered: the get takes the oldest item that matches. `wait: false` makes the get or put and does not wait for it: the task goes on at once.

| Key         | Type           | Default |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------- |
| `container` | text           | none    |
| `store`     | text           | none    |
| `amount`    | number or text | `1.0`   |
| `priority`  | None           | `0.0`   |
| `filter`    | text           | none    |
| `wait`      | boolean        | `true`  |

| `default` | text                       | none    |
| `weights` | mapping of names to number | none    |

## scenario

Type: list of [ScenarioStep](#scenario). Optional.

A `scenario` entry: at simulation time `at`, set `path` to `value`, publish a ground-truth record of `record`, or both.

`at` is seconds from the start of the run, or a duration such as `"10 min"`. A step with an `interrupt` interrupts the running instances of a task, as a task's `interrupt` does.

Type: mapping. Optional.

The `run` section.

`before` lists `!python` functions called with no arguments before the run starts, for setup such as creating topics or tables. `stop` ends the run before `until` at the next firing of a signal, `{signal: name}`, or when a condition first holds, `{condition: ...}`. `drain`, `true` or `{limit: 1 h}`, stops the arrivals at `until` and runs on until no entity is left in the model.

| Key                    | Type                       | Default      |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------ |
| `until`                | number or Duration         | none         |
| `before`               | list of !python reference  |              |
| `stop`                 | mapping of names to text   | none         |
| `drain`                | boolean or [Drain](#drain) | `false`      |
| `on_unhandled_failure` | `stop` or `continue`       | `"continue"` |

### Drain

A `run.drain` mapping: the longest a drain may run after `until`.

| Key     | Type               | Default |
| ------- | ------------------ | ------- |
| `limit` | number or Duration | none    |

# API Reference

## Simulation Context

### `SimulationContext(sim_id, factor=1.0, random_seed=None, logical_start_time=None, go_live_at=None, warmup=None, initial_time=0.0, lag_interval=None, timezone=None, strict=False, environment=None)`

Builder and Orchestrator for Event-Driven Digital Twins.

The `SimulationContext` implements the Builder Pattern to construct the foundational architecture of a Digital Twin. It acts as the central control plane, aggregating discrete machine capacities, continuous physical states (wear and tear), and statistical distributions into a unified `SimParameter` object.

Architectural Guarantees:

1. **Immutability During Configuration**: The underlying `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment` and its background asynchronous I/O threads are completely deferred until `.run()` is explicitly invoked. This prevents partial state leaks or unintended clock starts.
1. **One registry**: All registered configurations are flattened and managed by the internal `SimulationRegistry`, allowing external Kafka Admin commands to mutate these states safely during runtime.
1. **Deterministic Stochasticity**: The `Sampler` gives each distribution a random sequence of its own, made from `random_seed`, so a seeded run repeats exactly, and adding a distribution leaves the others' draws unchanged. A run without `random_seed` draws a seed and logs it, so it can be repeated.

Attributes:

| Name          | Type                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `sim_id`      | `str`                | The unique namespace for this simulation instance (e.g., 'HotRolling').                                                                                                                    |
| `factor`      | `float`              | The real-time synchronization multiplier. A factor of 1.0 syncs strictly with wall-clock time, while 0.0 executes instantly in a fast-forward loop (ideal for historical data processing). |
| `go_live_at`  | `Optional[datetime]` | Logical instant at which factor is replaced by real-time pacing, so one run can backfill history and then tail live.                                                                       |
| `warmup`      | `Optional[float]`    | The end of the warm-up, in simulation seconds.                                                                                                                                             |
| `random_seed` | `Optional[int]`      | The run's seed. When None, run() draws one, logs it and uses it; read it afterwards from sampler.seed.                                                                                     |
| `sampler`     | `Optional[Sampler]`  | The centralized Random Number Generator engine. Accessible to user-defined raw generators only after .run() is called.                                                                     |

Initializes the context builder with a designated namespace and temporal factor.

Source code in `src/desflow/core/context.py`

```python
def __init__(
    self,
    sim_id: str,
    factor: float = 1.0,
    random_seed: Optional[int] = None,
    logical_start_time: Optional[datetime] = None,
    go_live_at: Optional[datetime] = None,
    warmup: Union[float, str, None] = None,
    initial_time: Union[float, str] = 0.0,
    lag_interval: Union[float, str, None] = None,
    timezone: Optional[str] = None,
    strict: bool = False,
    environment: Optional[Type[DynamicRealtimeEnvironment]] = None,
):
    """
    Initializes the context builder with a designated namespace and temporal factor.

    Args:
        sim_id: The unique prefix for this group of parameters. All generated
            telemetry and event paths will be prefixed with this ID.
        factor: The real-time synchronization factor. Defaults to 1.0.
        random_seed: Optional seed for deterministic execution.
        logical_start_time: Optional override for the environment's base clock,
            forwarded to `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`. Crucial for historical
            backfilling (e.g., generating data from last week).
        go_live_at: Optional logical instant at which the run stops using `factor`
            and switches to real time, forwarded to `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`.
            With `factor=0.0` and a backdated `logical_start_time`, the history up
            to this instant is generated as fast as the machine allows and the rest
            arrives in real time, so a backfill and a live tail take one run.
        warmup: The end of the warm-up, in simulation seconds or as a duration
            such as `"10 min"`. No sink receives a record stamped before it, and
            the built-in statistics are reset at that time, so they measure the
            steady state only.
        initial_time: The simulation clock's starting value, in seconds or as a
            duration such as `"8 h"`, so event times, `sim_ts` and `until` are
            readings of a clock that starts there. Defaults to 0.
        lag_interval: Simulation seconds, or a duration such as `"10 s"`, between
            `system.simulation.lag_seconds` records, which measure how far the
            run is behind the wall clock. By default it is off at `factor` 0,
            where lag means nothing, and every simulation second otherwise; a
            run that goes live starts it then. 0 turns it off.
        timezone: An IANA time zone name, such as `"Australia/Melbourne"`, that
            record timestamps are written in, with their offset. By default the
            zone of `logical_start_time`, or UTC. A `logical_start_time` or
            `go_live_at` without an offset is read in it.
        strict: When True a paced step raises `RuntimeError` if the run is more
            than `factor` real seconds behind the wall clock, as SimPy's
            `RealtimeEnvironment` does. It is never checked at `factor` 0. False
            by default, unlike the low-level environment, because a live run
            whose sink blocks falls behind and should go on.
        environment: A subclass of `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment` that the run is
            built on, for a model that overrides `step`, `schedule` or `__init__`.
            A subclass that overrides `__init__` takes `**kwargs` and passes
            them on. One that overrides `step` or `schedule` calls `super()`.
            By default `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If `warmup` or `lag_interval` is negative or not a duration,
            `timezone` is not an IANA time zone name, or `environment` is not a
            subclass of `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`.
    """
    if environment is not None and not (
        isinstance(environment, type)
        and issubclass(environment, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment)
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            "environment must be a subclass of DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, "
            f"got {environment!r}"
        )
    self.sim_id = sim_id
    self.factor = factor
    self.strict = strict
    self.environment: Type[DynamicRealtimeEnvironment] = (
        environment or DynamicRealtimeEnvironment
    )
    self.random_seed = random_seed
    self.logical_start_time = logical_start_time
    self.go_live_at = go_live_at
    self.initial_time = _seconds(initial_time)
    self.warmup = None if warmup is None else _seconds(warmup)
    if self.warmup is not None and self.warmup < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"warmup must be 0 or more, got {warmup}")
    resolve_zone(timezone)  # an unknown name is refused here, not at run()
    self.timezone = timezone
    self.lag_interval = None if lag_interval is None else _seconds(lag_interval)
    if self.lag_interval is not None and self.lag_interval < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"lag_interval must be 0 or more, got {lag_interval}")

    # Builder State (Pre-Compilation)
    self._ingress_providers: List[Any] = []
    self._egress_providers: List[Any] = []
    # Aligned with _egress_providers by position. None means the provider
    # receives every record.
    self._egress_predicates: List[Optional[Callable[[dict], bool]]] = []
    # Aligned with _egress_providers by position. None falls back to the
    # context default set by with_batching.
    self._egress_batch_sizes: List[Optional[int]] = []
    self._egress_flush_intervals: List[Optional[float]] = []
    self._batch_size = 500
    self._flush_interval = 1.0
    self._max_queued_batches = 2000
    self._drain_stall_seconds = 30.0

    # Aligned with _egress_providers by position.
    self._egress_labels: List[bool] = []
    self._stats_level = DEFAULT_STATS_LEVEL
    self._stats_interval = DEFAULT_STATS_INTERVAL

    self._resources_config: Dict[str, CapacityConfig] = {}
    self._resource_queues: Dict[str, str] = {}
    self._resource_preempt: Dict[str, bool] = {}
    self._resource_queue_limits: Dict[str, Optional[int]] = {}
    self._resource_types: Dict[str, Optional[Type[ResourceBase]]] = {}
    self._breakdowns_config: Dict[str, BreakdownConfig] = {}
    self._scenario_steps: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    # Replayed arrivals: how to read each, and the rows left once read
    self._replays: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
    self._replay_rows: Dict[str, List[Row]] = {}
    self._replays_done: set = set()
    self._containers_config: Dict[str, CapacityConfig] = {}
    self._stores_config: Dict[str, CapacityConfig] = {}
    self._store_priority: Dict[str, bool] = {}
    self._store_types: Dict[str, Optional[Type[StoreBase]]] = {}
    self._container_types: Dict[str, Optional[Type[ContainerBase]]] = {}
    self._store_items: Dict[str, List[Any]] = {}
    self._services_config: Dict[str, DistributionConfig] = {}
    self._arrivals_config: Dict[str, DistributionConfig] = {}
    # Per arrival: the attributes each entity starts with, and the key function
    self._arrival_entities: Dict[
        str, Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Optional[Callable[[int], str]]]
    ] = {}
    # Per arrival given `spawn`: the task each of its entities starts
    self._arrival_spawns: Dict[str, str] = {}
    self._variables_config: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    # Tasks by name, with what run() checks before the clock starts
    self._tasks: Dict[str, Callable] = {}
    self._task_specs: Dict[str, TaskSpec] = {}
    self._signal_names: List[str] = []
    self._signal_once: Dict[str, bool] = {}
    # Each signal's `on:` actions, in normalized form, run when it fires
    self._signal_on: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    self._signals: Dict[str, Signal] = {}
    # Tasks whose instances need an end event, filled by _check_tasks: those a
    # `running` branch or `subscribe` names (_tracked), those a `fire from`
    # copies (_copied), and every task with `on:` actions (_ended, the union)
    self._tracked: set = set()
    self._copied: set = set()
    self._ended: set = set()
    # Task instances running now, by task, which interrupt() reaches
    self._running: Dict[str, List[TaskRun]] = {}
    # The positional arguments a YAML task's function takes after its id
    self._task_args: Tuple[Any, ...] = ()

    # Runtime State (Post-Compilation)
    self._env: Optional[DynamicRealtimeEnvironment] = None
    # True once start() has built and started everything, so a caller can tell
    # a value refused before the run from an error inside it
    self.started = False
    self.sampler: Optional[Sampler] = None
    self._resources_map: Dict[str, ResourceBase] = {}
    self._stores_map: Dict[str, DynamicStore] = {}
    self._containers_map: Dict[str, DynamicContainer] = {}
    self._entity_counters: Dict[str, "itertools.count[int]"] = {}
    self._instance_counters: Dict[str, "itertools.count[int]"] = {}
    self._startup_loops: List[Tuple[Callable, Optional[str]]] = []
    # The functions add_process started, which explain shows as opaque nodes
    self._processes: List[Callable] = []
    # What builds this model again, a blueprint path or a function, set by
    # from_yaml and load_context, so analyze(verify=True) can run a copy
    self._source: Any = None

    # Set by from_yaml from the blueprint's `run` section.
    self._default_until: Any = None
    self._default_stop: Any = None
    self._default_drain: Any = None
    self._default_unhandled: str = "continue"
    self._on_unhandled_failure: str = "continue"
    # The run's end, entities in the model, and the drain state, set by start()
    self._until: Any = None
    self._end: Optional[simpy.Event] = None
    self._end_done = False
    # The internal event at `until` that advance() stops at, made on first use
    self._limit_event: Optional[simpy.Event] = None
    self._closed = True
    self._in_system = 0
    self._draining = False
    self._finish_run: Optional[Callable[..., None]] = None
    self._arrival_processes: List[simpy.Process] = []
    self._before_run: List[Callable[[], Any]] = []
    # How the log tells a run without a seed to repeat itself, with `{seed}`
    self._repeat_hint: Optional[str] = None
    # Set by from_yaml for `desflow run --sample`: the events a preview prints
    # before it ends the run, and how many it has printed
    self._sample_limit: Optional[int] = None
    self._sample_seen = 0
```

##### `add_arrival(name, dist, *, rate=None, mean=None, std=None, low=None, value=None, high=None, mode=None, shape=None, scale=None, values=None, weights=None, edges=None, counts=None, attributes=None, key=None, spawn=None)`

Registers a statistical distribution defining the inter-arrival times of entities.

Each arrival starts a new entity, which `wait_for_arrival` returns. Its key, the record key of every event it causes, is the arrival name and a counter (`orders-1`, `orders-2`) unless `key` gives another.

```python
def add_arrival(
    self,
    name: str,
    dist: str,
    *,
    rate: Optional[float] = None,
    mean: Optional[float] = None,
    std: Optional[float] = None,
    low: Optional[float] = None,
    value: Optional[float] = None,
    high: Optional[float] = None,
    mode: Optional[float] = None,
    shape: Optional[float] = None,
    scale: Optional[float] = None,
    values: Optional[List[float]] = None,
    weights: Optional[List[float]] = None,
    edges: Optional[List[float]] = None,
    counts: Optional[List[float]] = None,
    attributes: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None,
    key: Optional[Callable[[int], str]] = None,
    spawn: Optional[str] = None,
) -> "SimulationContext":
    """
    Registers a statistical distribution defining the inter-arrival times of entities.

    Each arrival starts a new entity, which `wait_for_arrival` returns. Its key,
    the record key of every event it causes, is the arrival name and a counter
    (`orders-1`, `orders-2`) unless `key` gives another.

    Args:
        name: The internal identifier (e.g., 'orders').
        dist: The family, as for `add_service`.
        rate: Events per second, for exponential.
        mean: The mean, for normal, lognormal and truncated_normal.
        std: The standard deviation, for the same three (0 when not given).
        low: The lowest value, for truncated_normal, uniform and triangular.
        value: The time a constant distribution always gives.
        high: The highest value, for uniform and triangular.
        mode: The most likely value, for triangular.
        shape: The shape, for gamma and weibull.
        scale: The scale, for gamma and weibull.
        values: The values an empirical draws from, taken at load.
        weights: One weight per empirical value.
        edges: The bin edges of an empirical histogram.
        counts: One count per empirical histogram bin.
        attributes: The attributes each entity starts with, read in conditions
            as `attr.<name>`. Each entity gets its own copy.
        key: A function of the entity's counter, from 1, returning its key.
        spawn: The task each arrival starts, with the arrival's entity and the
            task's next instance id, as YAML's `spawn` key does. None leaves
            the arrival to an `arrival_loop` written by hand.

    Returns:
        SimulationContext: The current instance for method chaining.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the family is unknown, or a parameter is missing, out of
            range or not one the family takes. A `spawn` naming no task is
            refused when the run starts.
    """
    params = {
        k: v for k, v in locals().items() if k not in ("attributes", "key", "spawn")
    }
    self._arrivals_config[name] = _distribution(dist, params)
    self._arrival_entities[name] = (dict(attributes or {}), key)
    self._add_spawn(name, spawn)
    return self
```

##### `add_arrival_replay(name, source, *, time='time', unit='s', fields='all', on_invalid='error', attributes=None, key=None, spawn=None)`

Registers an arrival taken from recorded rows instead of a distribution.

Each row becomes one arrival at its recorded time, in the order given, and its fields become the entity's attributes. `wait_for_arrival(name)` returns the wait for the next row, so an arrival loop is written as for any other arrival. Rows at equal times arrive at that time in their order; rows at or after `until` never arrive; after the last row the arrival stops, with one INFO line. The rows are read and checked when the run starts.

Parameters:

| Name         | Type                                            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                            | Default    |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------- |
| `name`       | `str`                                           | The arrival's name.                                                                                                                                                                                    | *required* |
| `source`     | `Union[str, Path, Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]]]` | A CSV or Parquet file (Parquet needs the parquet extra), or an iterable of mappings.                                                                                                                   | *required* |
| `time`       | `str`                                           | The column of each row's time.                                                                                                                                                                         | `'time'`   |
| `unit`       | `str`                                           | ms, s, min or h from the start of the run, or timestamp for a date and time, which arrives when the run's records carry that time: logical_start_time is simulation time 0, whatever the initial_time. | `'s'`      |
| `fields`     | `Union[str, List[str]]`                         | The columns each entity carries, or all.                                                                                                                                                               | `'all'`    |
| `on_invalid` | `str`                                           | error refuses a row with no valid time; skip leaves it out with a warning.                                                                                                                             | `'error'`  |
| `attributes` | `Optional[Mapping[str, Any]]`                   | Attributes every entity starts with; a row's fields of the same name replace them.                                                                                                                     | `None`     |
| `key`        | `Optional[Callable[[int], str]]`                | A function of the entity's counter, from 1, returning its key.                                                                                                                                         | `None`     |
| `spawn`      | `Optional[str]`                                 | The task each row starts, as for add_arrival.                                                                                                                                                          | `None`     |

Returns:

| Name                | Type                | Description                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `SimulationContext` | `SimulationContext` | The current instance for method chaining. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                                              |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ValueError` | If unit or on_invalid is unknown. A spawn naming no task is refused when the run starts. |

Source code in `src/desflow/core/context.py`

```python
def add_arrival_replay(
    self,
    name: str,
    source: Union[str, Path, Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]]],
    *,
    time: str = "time",
    unit: str = "s",
    fields: Union[str, List[str]] = "all",
    on_invalid: str = "error",
    attributes: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None,
    key: Optional[Callable[[int], str]] = None,
    spawn: Optional[str] = None,
) -> "SimulationContext":
    """
    Registers an arrival taken from recorded rows instead of a distribution.

    Each row becomes one arrival at its recorded time, in the order given, and
    its fields become the entity's attributes. `wait_for_arrival(name)` returns
    the wait for the next row, so an arrival loop is written as for any other
    arrival. Rows at equal times arrive at that time in their order; rows at or
    after `until` never arrive; after the last row the arrival stops, with one
    INFO line. The rows are read and checked when the run starts.

    Args:
        name: The arrival's name.
        source: A CSV or Parquet file (Parquet needs the `parquet` extra), or
            an iterable of mappings.
        time: The column of each row's time.
        unit: `ms`, `s`, `min` or `h` from the start of the run, or `timestamp`
            for a date and time, which arrives when the run's records carry
            that time: `logical_start_time` is simulation time 0, whatever
            the `initial_time`.
        fields: The columns each entity carries, or `all`.
        on_invalid: `error` refuses a row with no valid time; `skip` leaves it
            out with a warning.
        attributes: Attributes every entity starts with; a row's fields of the
            same name replace them.
        key: A function of the entity's counter, from 1, returning its key.
        spawn: The task each row starts, as for `add_arrival`.

    Returns:
        SimulationContext: The current instance for method chaining.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If `unit` or `on_invalid` is unknown. A `spawn` naming no
            task is refused when the run starts.
    """
    if unit not in UNITS and unit != "timestamp":
        raise ValueError(
            f"unit must be one of {', '.join([*UNITS, 'timestamp'])}, got '{unit}'"
        )
    if on_invalid not in ("error", "skip"):
        raise ValueError(f"on_invalid must be error or skip, got '{on_invalid}'")
    self._replays[name] = dict(
        source=source, time=time, unit=unit, fields=fields, on_invalid=on_invalid
    )
    self._arrival_entities[name] = (dict(attributes or {}), key)
    self._add_spawn(name, spawn)
    return self
```

##### `add_breakdown(resource, time_to_failure, repair, work='interrupt')`

Makes a resource break down at random and be repaired.

The failure clock runs on calendar time: after each repair, or the start, the time to the next failure is drawn, busy or idle. While the resource is down its capacity is 0, its `current_cap` keeps the planned value, and a change to it during the repair sets the capacity the resource returns to. Each failure and repair publishes an event keyed by the resource's name, `{"status": "down", "reason": "failure"}` and `{"status": "repaired", ...}`. The two distributions are registry paths, `<sim_id>.breakdown.<resource>.time_to_failure` and `.repair`.

Parameters:

| Name              | Type                | Description                                                                                                          | Default       |
| ----------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `resource`        | `str`               | The resource's name.                                                                                                 | *required*    |
| `time_to_failure` | `Mapping[str, Any]` | A distribution, such as {"dist": "weibull", "shape": 1.5, "scale": 3600}.                                            | *required*    |
| `repair`          | `Mapping[str, Any]` | A distribution, such as {"dist": "exponential", "rate": 0.01}.                                                       | *required*    |
| `work`            | `str`               | interrupt (the default) interrupts the tasks being served, which follow their on_interrupt; finish lets them finish. | `'interrupt'` |

Returns:

| Name                | Type                | Description                               |
| ------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `SimulationContext` | `SimulationContext` | The current instance for method chaining. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                           |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------- |
| `ValueError` | If a distribution or work is invalid. |

Source code in `src/desflow/core/context.py`

) -> "SimulationContext":
    """
    Makes a resource break down at random and be repaired.

    The failure clock runs on calendar time: after each repair, or the start,
    the time to the next failure is drawn, busy or idle. While the resource is
    down its capacity is 0, its `current_cap` keeps the planned value, and a
    change to it during the repair sets the capacity the resource returns to.
    Each failure and repair publishes an event keyed by the resource's name,
    `{"status": "down", "reason": "failure"}` and `{"status": "repaired", ...}`.
    The two distributions are registry paths,
    `<sim_id>.breakdown.<resource>.time_to_failure` and `.repair`.

    Args:
        resource: The resource's name.
        time_to_failure: A distribution, such as
            `{"dist": "weibull", "shape": 1.5, "scale": 3600}`.
